BadRequest.description: Bad request — the connector configuration was well-formed but could not be established against the UEM platform. Error code: `UEM_CONNECTION_FAILED` — the connection test against the supplied URL and credentials failed.

errors.description: A connector already exists for the customer with an incompatible UEM vendor.

Conflict.description: Conflict — the request cannot proceed against the current state of the tenant's connectors. Error codes: `CONNECTOR_DISABLED` — the connector is disabled (`triggerSync`, `deployActivationProfile`); `CONNECTOR_CONFIG_ALREADY_EXISTS` — the tenant already has a connector whose UEM vendor cannot coexist with the requested one, only Jamf Pro and Wizy may coexist (`createConnector`); `UNSUPPORTED_UEM_VERSION` — the UEM platform reported a version this integration does not support (`createConnector`); `MULTIPLE_ACTIVATION_PROFILES` — the tenant has more than one active activation profile, so the deployment target is ambiguous (`deployActivationProfile`). Not every code applies to every operation — check the individual operation's description.

errors.description: No activation profile found for customer.

NotFound.description: Not found — the referenced connector or resource does not exist. Error codes: `NOT_FOUND` — the referenced connector or resource does not exist for the tenant; `NO_ACTIVATION_PROFILE` — the tenant has no active activation profile to deploy (only emittable by `deployActivationProfile`). Not every code applies to every operation — check the individual operation's description.

errors.description: The UEM platform is currently unavailable

ServiceUnavailable.description: Service unavailable — the UEM platform could not be reached or returned an error. Retry later. Error code: `UEM_UNAVAILABLE`.

errors.description: The sync could not be dispatched. Please retry.

SyncDispatchRejected.description: Service unavailable — the sync could not be dispatched because the service's sync workers are saturated or the instance is shutting down. No sync run is left in progress, so the request can be retried. Error code: `SYNC_DISPATCH_REJECTED`.

errors.description: Connector 'conn-abc123' is not connected to the UEM platform

UnprocessableEntity.description:
Unprocessable entity. This API returns `422` for **both** schema-level and business-rule failures. Error codes: `VALIDATION_FAILED` — malformed JSON, a missing or mistyped required field, or a constraint violation (the `field` property identifies the offending body field where known); `CONNECTOR_NOT_CONNECTED` — the connector's credentials are not valid against the UEM platform; `CONNECTOR_MISCONFIGURED` — the UEM platform rejected the connector configuration.
Note that connector creation can also fail with `400` when the connection test itself fails — see the `400` response on that operation.

ActivationProfileDeployRequest.description: Request to deploy activation profile configuration profiles to UEM

platform.description: The device platform type for the configuration profile

uem.description: The UEM platform to deploy profiles to

uemGroups.description: Optional UEM groups to scope the deployment to. If omitted or empty, deploys to all UEM groups.

ApiError.description: Standard error object returned for all failed requests.

errors.description: The individual problems with the request

traceId.description: Correlation identifier for the failed request

ApiErrorEntry.description: A single problem with the request.

description.example: Connector 'conn-abc123' is not connected to the UEM platform

field.description: The request field the error relates to, when applicable

ConnectorConfig.description:
Connector configuration. Contains both core fields and vendor-specific fields.
Additional vendor-specific properties may appear alongside the documented ones.
Secret fields (credentials) are write-only and are never returned.

concurrentSyncEnabled.description: Whether this connector may sync concurrently with other connectors

connected.description: Whether the connector is currently connected to the UEM platform

connectorDeviceTypeAlias.description: Internal device-type discriminator for this connector's vendor

customerId.description: Identifier of the customer that owns this connector configuration

deviceRiskTagging.description: Whether device risk levels are sent back to the UEM platform

deviceUnmanagedThreshold.description:
Number of consecutive syncs a device may be absent from the UEM platform before it is
treated as unmanaged. `0` disables the grace period.

emmTaggingSupported.description: Whether the UEM platform supports receiving device tags from JSC

enabled.description: Whether the connector is enabled for synchronization

id.description: Unique identifier for the connector configuration

isoCountry.description: ISO country code for the UEM instance, when applicable

nextScheduledSync.description: Timestamp of the next scheduled sync (ISO 8601)

previousSyncStart.description: Timestamp when the previous sync started (ISO 8601)

tenantId.description:
Platform tenant identifier of the Jamf Pro instance this connector syncs with, when it was created by naming one. Null for a connector created from caller-supplied credentials.

Load-bearing beyond information: `authStrategy` reads back as `JAMF_PRO_OAUTH` whichever way the connector was created, so this field is the only thing in the response that distinguishes the two forms. A consumer reconstructing a connector's configuration — Terraform importing one it did not create, say — has nothing else to key on. Note that a tenant-named connector also reports a `deviceSyncAuth.clientId`, the credential Jamf Security Cloud provisioned for itself, so the presence of credentials cannot serve as the signal. Restored from the wire (probed 2026-08-28), where the published spec omits it.

uemVersion.description: Version of the UEM instance the connector is talking to — for a Jamf Pro connector, the Jamf Pro version. Reported by the connector rather than configured, and useful for surfacing what the integration is actually connected to. Restored from the wire (probed 2026-08-28), where the published spec omits it.

ConnectorCreateRequest.description:
Request to create a connector. Contains the UEM server connection details. Vendor-specific
fields may also be included; the `vendor` field determines which are applicable. Secret
fields (credentials) are write-only and are never returned in responses.

`JAMF_PRO` is not accepted here — it has a dedicated fully typed contract, see
`JamfProConnectorCreateRequest`.

isoCountry.description: ISO country code for the UEM instance, when applicable

ConnectorCreateRequestBody.description:
The connector to create. The `vendor` field selects the contract: `JAMF_PRO` uses the fully
typed `JamfProConnectorCreateRequest`; every other vendor uses the generic
`ConnectorCreateRequest`.

results.description: The connectors for the requested page

totalCount.description: Total number of connectors across all pages

CreatedResource.description: Identifier and location of a newly created resource.

href.description:
Location of the created resource, as a path relative to the API base URL the request was
made against.

It is deliberately relative rather than absolute, and it does not repeat the tenant scope
segment: connector-service is customer-scoped downstream of the gateway and never
receives the `tenantId` or the external host, so it cannot construct the fully qualified
tenant-scoped URL. Resolve it against the same base URL — including the tenant scope
prefix the publishing pipeline injects — that was used for the `POST`.

DeviceFieldMappings.description:
Controls which UEM attribute each JSC device field is populated from. Each value is an
enum of UEM attribute names whose members are vendor-specific, so the accepted values for
a given key depend on the connector's `vendor`. The Google connector accepts no mappings.

deviceNameMapping.description: UEM attribute the device name is read from

phoneNumberMapping.description: UEM attribute the phone number is read from

userIdMapping.description: UEM attribute the user identifier is read from

userNameMapping.description: UEM attribute the user name is read from

DeviceSyncAuth.description: Credentials the connector authenticates to the UEM instance with, as read back off a connector. Restored from the wire (probed 2026-08-21, re-verified 2026-08-31) because the published spec omits `deviceSyncAuth` from the *response* schema; the request side is upstream's own `JamfProCredentials` as of v1882, which carries the same four members. Which of them apply depends on `authStrategy` — OAuth strategies use `clientId`/`clientSecret`, basic-auth strategies use `username`/`password`. Secrets are write-only and never returned; a read reports only `clientId`, `username` and an `empty` flag, and for an `M2M`-provisioned connector the `clientId` is the one Jamf Security Cloud minted for itself.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID. For `JAMF_PRO_OAUTH`, the client ID of an API integration on the target Jamf Pro instance.

clientSecret.description: OAuth client secret paired with `clientId`. Write-only — never returned on a read.

password.description: Password paired with `username`. Write-only — never returned on a read.

EmailMapping.description:
How the device email is derived. `EMAIL_ADDRESS` uses the UEM email attribute directly;
any other type reads from that attribute and optionally decorates it into an address.

Vendors that support the `CUSTOM` type carry an additional `fieldName` property naming the UEM
attribute to read. It is not documented as a property here because the vendors that do not
support `CUSTOM` do not emit it at all, and ADG-125 requires every documented field to be
present in every response.

fieldPrefix.description: Prepended to the resolved value. Ignored when `type` is `EMAIL_ADDRESS`.

fieldSuffix.description:
Appended to the resolved value to form a full address; an `@` is inserted when the
suffix does not already start with one. Ignored when `type` is `EMAIL_ADDRESS`.

type.description: UEM attribute the email is derived from

useOnlyIfEmailMissing.description: Apply this mapping only when the UEM email attribute is empty, rather than always.

EnablementRequest.description: Desired enablement state for a connector.

enabled.description: Whether the connector should be enabled for synchronization

GroupMapping.description:
A single UEM-group-to-JSC-group assignment.

Both property names retain legacy internal product names (`emm` for UEM, `wandera` for
JSC). They are the names the service serializes and accepts today, so they are documented
as-is; renaming them would break existing callers.

emmGroupId.description: Group identifier in the UEM platform

wanderaGroupId.description: JSC group identifier devices in the UEM group are assigned to

GroupSettings.description: Group mapping configuration. Maps UEM groups to JSC groups.

defaultGroupId.description: JSC group that devices are assigned to when no explicit mapping matches

groupMappingEnabled.description: Whether group mapping is applied during sync

groupMappings.description:
Explicit UEM-group-to-JSC-group assignments. Replaces the existing set on update;
send an empty array to clear all mappings.

JamfProConnectorCreateRequest.description:
Connector creation request for Jamf Pro.

The `authStrategy` field selects how JSC authenticates to Jamf Pro and determines which
further fields are required:

- `JAMF_PRO_OAUTH` — provide `deviceSyncAuth.clientId` and `deviceSyncAuth.clientSecret`
  (Jamf Pro API-role OAuth client credentials).
- `BASIC` — provide `deviceSyncAuth.username` and `deviceSyncAuth.password`.
- `M2M` — provide `tenantId`; `deviceSyncAuth` must be omitted (JSC authenticates through the
  shared machine-to-machine trust rather than per-connector credentials).

The credential fields (`deviceSyncAuth.password`, `deviceSyncAuth.clientSecret`) are
write-only. `tenantId` is likewise write-only: it is accepted on creation but not returned
in responses. Write-only fields are never echoed back in any response.

authStrategy.description:
Authentication strategy used to connect to Jamf Pro. See the schema description for the
fields each strategy requires.

isoCountry.description: ISO country code for the UEM instance, when applicable

tenantId.description:
Jamf Pro tenant identifier. Required when `authStrategy` is `M2M`; must be omitted for
the other strategies.

JamfProCredentials.description:
Jamf Pro connection credentials. Provide the OAuth pair (`clientId` + `clientSecret`) when
`authStrategy` is `JAMF_PRO_OAUTH`, or the basic pair (`username` + `password`) when
`authStrategy` is `BASIC`. Omit entirely for `M2M`.

clientId.description: Jamf Pro API-role OAuth client id (JAMF_PRO_OAUTH strategy)

clientSecret.description: Jamf Pro API-role OAuth client secret (JAMF_PRO_OAUTH strategy)

LatestSync.description:
Summary of the connector's most recent sync run, embedded in `ConnectorConfig`. The
containing `latestSync` property is `null` until the connector has run its first sync.

This is **not** the same shape as the `SyncRun` entries returned by
`GET /connectors/{configId}/sync/runs`: it carries `lastSeen` and `errorDetails`, and has no
per-run device counters, because the connector record keeps only the current transaction's
state and not its tallies. Use the sync-runs endpoint for run history and counts.

`startedUtcMs` and `finishedUtcMs` are retained, deprecated epoch-millisecond duplicates of
the ISO-8601 `started` and `finished`. They are still emitted for existing consumers; new
consumers should read the ISO-8601 fields.

finished.description: Timestamp when sync completed (ISO 8601), null if still running

finishedUtcMs.description: `finished` as epoch milliseconds. Deprecated duplicate — prefer the ISO-8601 `finished`.

lastSeen.description:
Timestamp of the last progress heartbeat from the running sync (ISO 8601), used to
detect stalled syncs

startedUtcMs.description: `started` as epoch milliseconds. Deprecated duplicate — prefer the ISO-8601 `started`.

transactionId.description:
Unique identifier for this sync run. Always present when `latestSync` itself is present:
it is the identifier of the underlying sync transaction, and the whole object is null
when there is no transaction.

SyncConfig.description:
Sync configuration settings as returned in responses. Response-only: the corresponding
update request carries these two settings as **top-level** `autoDeviceDeletion` and
`disableSyncOnAuthError` fields on `SyncSettings`, not nested under `syncConfig`.

autoDeviceDeletion.description: Auto-deletion policy for devices removed from the UEM platform

disableSyncOnAuthError.description: Whether to automatically disable sync after repeated authentication failures

SyncErrorDetails.description:
Why the most recent sync failed. Always present, with null members when the sync did not
fail.

SyncRun.description: Details of a single sync run.

deleted.description: Number of devices removed during this run

errored.description: Number of devices that encountered errors during this run

finished.description: Timestamp when sync completed (ISO 8601), null if still running

synced.description: Number of devices synced (added or updated) during this run

transactionId.description: Unique identifier for this sync run

results.description: The sync runs for the requested page

totalCount.description: Total number of sync runs across all pages

SyncSettings.description:
Sync settings update request. Vendor-specific fields may also be included.
The `vendor` field in the body determines which additional fields are applicable.

This is a **full replacement**, not a patch: omitted optional fields are reset to their
defaults rather than left unchanged. Send the complete desired state.

Note the asymmetry with the response: `autoDeviceDeletion` and `disableSyncOnAuthError` are
top-level here, but are returned nested under `syncConfig` on `ConnectorConfig`.

autoDeviceDeletion.description: Auto-deletion policy for devices removed from the UEM platform

concurrentSyncEnabled.description:
Whether this connector may sync several devices concurrently, for faster inventory updates.

Absent from the published spec's update request while present on the response, and writable — a `PUT` carrying `false` persists (wire-verified 2026-08-28). Because the update is a full replacement, a request built from the unpatched spec could not express the field and therefore reset it to `true` on every write, silently discarding an operator's choice.

deviceRiskTagging.description: Whether device risk levels are sent back to UEM

deviceUnmanagedThreshold.description:
Number of consecutive syncs a device may be absent from the UEM platform before it is
treated as unmanaged. `0` disables the grace period.

disableSyncOnAuthError.description: Whether to automatically disable sync after repeated authentication failures

vendor.description: UEM vendor name — determines the shape of vendor-specific fields

oauth2.description: Obtain an access token by calling the API Gateway's token endpoint using the OAuth2 client-credentials flow.

info.description: API for managing UEM Connect connectors
info.title: JSC UEM Connect API (STAGE)

post.description:
Deploys Jamf Security configuration profiles to the UEM platform for the specified
activation profile. This is the final step of automated UEM Connect onboarding.

**Note:** The activation profile code is obtained from the Jamf Security setup flow and is
not issued by the UEM Connect API. This operation is idempotent.

Requires a connector that is connected to its UEM platform and not disabled — otherwise
`422 CONNECTOR_NOT_CONNECTED` or `409 CONNECTOR_DISABLED` respectively. Returns
`409 MULTIPLE_ACTIVATION_PROFILES` if the tenant has more than one active activation profile
and the deployment target is ambiguous.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:update`
post.summary: Deploy Jamf Security configuration profiles to UEM

get.description:
Returns the connectors configured for the tenant.

**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:read`

post.description:
Creates a new connector for the tenant. On success returns the identifier of the created
connector together with an `href` locating it, as a path relative to the base URL the
request was made against.

A tenant may hold only one connector, with the single exception that Jamf Pro and Wizy may
coexist. Requesting any other second connector fails with `409 CONNECTOR_CONFIG_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

Creation runs a connection test against the supplied URL and credentials. A failing test
yields `400 UEM_CONNECTION_FAILED`, and a UEM platform running an unsupported version yields
`409 UNSUPPORTED_UEM_VERSION`.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:create`

delete.description:
Deletes the connector identified by `configId` and all of its data.

**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:delete`

get.description:
Returns the connector identified by `configId`.

**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:read`

delete.description:
Disables the specified connector to pause data synchronization between JSC and the UEM
platform. This operation is idempotent — disabling an already-disabled connector succeeds.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:delete`

put.description:
Sets the enablement state of the specified connector. Send `enabled: true` to resume data
synchronization between JSC and the UEM platform, or `enabled: false` to pause it. This
operation is idempotent.

Enabling reaches out to the UEM platform to switch the integration back on, so it can fail
with `503` when that platform is unreachable. Disabling tolerates such a failure and still
succeeds locally, which is why `DELETE` on this path does not document `503`.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:update`

get.description:
Returns the current connector configuration including sync settings.

**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:read`

put.description:
Updates the sync settings for the specified connector. Supported settings vary by UEM vendor.
Updated settings take effect on the next sync operation.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:update`

get.description:
Retrieves paginated sync run history for the specified connector, ordered from newest to
oldest.

This operation queries sync history directly and does not verify that `configId` refers to
an existing connector, so an unknown `configId` returns `200` with an empty result set
rather than `404`.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:read`

post.description:
Triggers a new sync operation for the specified connector. The sync runs asynchronously;
this endpoint returns immediately (`202 Accepted`). Poll `GET /sync/runs` to monitor
progress.

Conditions:
- Connector must be enabled (not disabled) — otherwise `409 Conflict`.
- Connector must be connected (credentials valid) — otherwise `422 Unprocessable Entity`.

Triggering is fire-and-forget: if a sync is already running the request is still accepted
(`202 Accepted`) and coalesced, rather than rejected.

Dispatching the run is a separate step from accepting the request and can be refused when the
service is at capacity — see `503 Service Unavailable`.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:update`

delete.description:
Requests cancelation of the currently running sync operation for the specified connector.
Cancelation is best-effort; the sync may complete before it takes effect. Check status via
`GET /sync/runs`.

This operation is unconditionally successful: it applies a conditional update that matches
only a running sync, so `204` is returned whether a sync was canceled, no sync was running,
or `configId` does not exist. It never returns `404`.


**Required Permissions:** `uem-connect:update`

204.description: Cancelation requested (or no sync was running)
